config.title: TanStack Query Basics

intro.title: TanStack Query Basics
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React app that fetches and displays a list of posts from a mock API using TanStack Query. You will learn the core concept of server-state management, which handles fetching, caching, and updating data without manual state logic. The main technologies involved are React with TypeScript, the TanStack Query library (via @tanstack/react-query), and a mock API service. By the end, you'll understand how to set up a QueryClient, use the useQuery hook to fetch data, and display it in your components efficiently.
intro.usecase: TanStack Query is essential for building modern data-driven applications where real-time updates and efficient server state management are critical. You'll see this pattern in e-commerce product listings that need to stay synchronized with inventory, social media feeds that update with new posts, and dashboard analytics that refresh with live metrics. As a developer, you'll use TanStack Query to handle loading states, error handling, caching, and background refetching without manually managing complex state logic. This approach ensures users always see current data while maintaining optimal performance across network conditions.

objectives: Install and configure TanStack Query in a React TypeScript project using npm or yarn
Implement the QueryClientProvider component to wrap the application and provide query functionality
Define a QueryClient instance with default options for managing server state
Use the useQuery hook to fetch data from an API endpoint in a React component
Apply TypeScript generics to type the data returned by useQuery for type safety
Handle loading states by accessing the isLoading property from useQuery return values
Control error states by accessing the isError and error properties from useQuery return values
Utilize the data property from useQuery to display fetched information in JSX
Construct query keys as arrays to uniquely identify and cache query data
Execute query invalidation using the queryClient.invalidateQueries method to refresh data
Implement the useMutation hook to perform POST, PUT, or DELETE operations
Modify component UI based on mutation status (loading, success, error) using returned properties

steps.title: Import React and necessary hooks
steps.instruction: Import React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the useState hook from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and useState from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have an import statement for React and useState from 'react'.
successCriteria: The import statement must include both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState from 'react'. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the useState hook for state management.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the import statement needs both React and useState from 'react'. Make sure you're importing them correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import both React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Import TanStack Query core packages
steps.hint: Add an import statement at the top of your file to bring in these two core TanStack Query components.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing from a package
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
steps.seedCode:
// Import React and useState from 'react' here
// Import QueryClient and QueryClientProvider from '@tanstack/react-query' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The file will have both React imports and TanStack Query imports ready for use.
successCriteria: The import statement for QueryClient and QueryClientProvider from '@tanstack/react-query' is correctly added.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the core TanStack Query packages. QueryClient manages the cache and state, while QueryClientProvider makes it available to your React components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your import statement. Make sure you're importing both QueryClient and QueryClientProvider from '@tanstack/react-query'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement for TanStack Query packages is missing or incorrect. You need to import QueryClient and QueryClientProvider from '@tanstack/react-query'.

steps.title: Import TanStack Query hooks
steps.instruction: Add an import statement for the useQuery hook from '@tanstack/react-query'.
steps.hint: Import the useQuery hook from the same package you imported QueryClient and QueryClientProvider from.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing a hook from a package
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';
steps.expectedOutcome: The useQuery hook will be available for data fetching operations in your component.
successCriteria: The import statement for useQuery from '@tanstack/react-query' should be added correctly.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the useQuery hook, which is essential for fetching data with TanStack Query.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing useQuery from '@tanstack/react-query'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement for useQuery from '@tanstack/react-query' is missing or incorrect.

steps.title: Create QueryClient instance
steps.instruction: Create a new QueryClient instance using `new QueryClient()` and assign it to a variable named `queryClient`.
steps.hint: Use the QueryClient constructor imported in step 2 to create an instance.
steps.analogousExample:
// Create a QueryClient instance
const queryClient = new QueryClient();
steps.expectedOutcome: A QueryClient instance is created and stored in a variable named `queryClient`.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a QueryClient instance. This client will manage all your query caching and state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're creating a QueryClient instance with `new QueryClient()` and assigning it to a variable named `queryClient`.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create a QueryClient instance using the constructor and store it in a variable named `queryClient`.

steps.title: Create main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App with proper TypeScript typing that returns a JSX element.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function called App that returns a JSX element (like a div). Remember to add the return type : JSX.Element for TypeScript.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined with TypeScript typing and returns a JSX element.
successCriteria: The code should contain a component named App (function or arrow function) that returns a JSX element and has proper TypeScript typing (e.g., return type : JSX.Element).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the App component with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but it might be missing the TypeScript return type or the JSX element. Ensure the component is named App and returns a JSX element with the correct typing.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component is not correctly defined. Make sure to create a functional component named App that returns a JSX element and includes TypeScript typing.

steps.title: Wrap app with QueryClientProvider
steps.instruction: In your App component, wrap the existing content with the QueryClientProvider component and pass the QueryClient instance as the client prop.
steps.hint: Use JSX to wrap your component's return value with <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}> and close it with </QueryClientProvider>.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now returns JSX wrapped in QueryClientProvider, making the QueryClient instance available to all child components that use TanStack Query hooks.
successCriteria: The App component's return statement should be wrapped with <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}> and </QueryClientProvider>, using the queryClient instance created earlier.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wrapped your app with QueryClientProvider, which provides the QueryClient context to your entire application. This is essential for TanStack Query hooks to work properly.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there's something missing. Make sure you're wrapping the entire return value with QueryClientProvider and passing the queryClient instance as the client prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to wrap your JSX with QueryClientProvider and pass the queryClient instance as a prop. Check the example for the correct structure.

steps.title: Create data fetching function
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, create an async function named 'fetchPosts' that fetches data from the public JSONPlaceholder API endpoint 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts'.
steps.hint: Define an async function that uses the fetch API to get data from the URL and returns the parsed JSON response.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have an async function named 'fetchPosts' that fetches data from the JSONPlaceholder API and returns the parsed JSON data.
successCriteria: The function must be defined inside the App component, be named 'fetchPosts', be async, use fetch to call the API endpoint, and return the parsed JSON data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created an async data fetching function. This function will be used by TanStack Query to fetch posts data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function is async, uses the correct API endpoint, and properly returns the parsed JSON data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't meet all requirements. Check that it's async, uses fetch with the correct URL, and returns the parsed JSON data.

steps.title: Initialize loading state
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use the useState hook to create a loading state variable with boolean type. Initialize it to false.
steps.hint: Call useState<boolean>(false) to create a loading state variable and its setter function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have a loading state variable that can be used to manually track loading status.
successCriteria: The code should include a useState call with boolean type annotation, initialized to false, inside the App component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a loading state variable with boolean type.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've used useState with boolean type and initialized it to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The loading state wasn't properly initialized. Remember to use useState<boolean>(false) inside the App component.

steps.title: Use useQuery hook for data fetching
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, call the useQuery hook to fetch posts. Use the query key ['posts'] and the fetchPosts function as the query function. Destructure isLoading, error, and data from the result.
steps.hint: The useQuery hook takes an object with queryKey and queryFn properties. Destructure the returned object to get the loading state, error, and data.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useQuery hook is implemented with proper query key and function, and the isLoading, error, and data variables are destructured.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the useQuery hook with proper query configuration and destructured the essential properties.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but some elements are missing. Make sure you're calling useQuery with both queryKey and queryFn, and destructuring isLoading, error, and data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useQuery hook implementation is incomplete or incorrect. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Create basic component structure
steps.instruction: Add a container div with an h1 heading to your App component's return statement. The h1 should display 'TanStack Query Basics'.
steps.hint: Inside the return statement, wrap the existing h1 with a div element to create a container.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component returns a div container with an h1 heading displaying 'TanStack Query Basics'.
successCriteria: The return statement contains a div element
The div contains an h1 element
The h1 displays the text 'TanStack Query Basics'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the basic component structure with a container div and heading.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both the container div and the h1 heading with the correct text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The structure doesn't match what was requested. Check that you have a div container with an h1 heading inside.

steps.title: Display loading and error states
steps.instruction: In your App component, add conditional rendering to display loading and error messages based on the isLoading and isError properties from the useQuery result.
steps.hint: Use the isLoading and isError properties from the useQuery result object to conditionally render different UI elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will conditionally render loading and error messages before displaying the fetched data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented conditional rendering for both loading and error states. This ensures users get appropriate feedback while data is being fetched.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've made progress with conditional rendering, but check if you're handling both isLoading and isError states properly. Make sure you're using the correct properties from the useQuery result.
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional rendering for loading and error states isn't quite right. Remember to check both isLoading and isError properties from the useQuery result and render appropriate messages for each state.

steps.title: Display fetched data
steps.instruction: In your App component, display the fetched posts data when the query is successful. Render the posts array by mapping through them and showing each post's title.
steps.hint: Access the data from the useQuery result and use the map method to render each post. Remember to add a unique key prop to each rendered post.
steps.expectedOutcome: The app will display a list of post titles when the data fetching is successful.
successCriteria: Include a key prop for each post
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully displayed the fetched posts data. The app now shows a list of post titles when the query succeeds.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're accessing the data from useQuery and mapping through the posts array to render each title with a key prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on displaying the fetched data. You need to access the data from useQuery and map through the posts to render each title.
